newsitem.title: PERU: Glencore says likely to bid for Peru mines in May.
newsitem.headline: Glencore says likely to bid for Peru mines in May.

text.p: Switzerland's Glencore International, which formally started bidding earlier Monday for the La Oroya metallurgic complex, said it was also likely to enter the auction of two Peruvian mines in May.

Asked if Glencore would bid to buy Peru's state-owned Andaychagua and San Cristobal mines -- on the privatization slate as a single asset -- the company's representative in Peru, Ricardo Briceno, said: "Probably."

Last year, San Cristobal produced 680,000 dry tonnes of ore containing zinc, lead, copper and silver while Andaychagua produced about 395,000 dry tonnes of ore with silver, lead and zinc. The two production units are close to one another and lie 50 kilometers (30 miles) from La Oroya -- a huge complex of refineries and smelters.
"We are also analyzing the possibility of taking part in the auctions of the port terminals of (state oil company) Petroperu," Briceno told reporters.
The Glencore official spoke during a presentation of his company's technical credentials at the start of formal bidding for La Oroya, whose new owner will be decided April 18.
Mexico's Industrias Penoles S.A. and Doe Run Co of the U.S. also presented technical credentials to bid for La Oroya.
The asset sales are part of Peru's ongoing, piecemeal privatization of state mining company Centromin, which plans to sell more mines, hydroelectric plants and polymetallic mineral deposits.
